title: World outdoor public stair climbs — strict wave-two research dossier

method.inclusion: Named outdoor public stairway or stair street where the climb itself is the experience, normally about 40+ steps or 10+ metres of ascent, or with exceptional documented architectural or social significance.
method.source_gate: At least two useful sources per retained row, including an official, municipal, heritage, destination, land-manager or first-party source.
method.confidence_gate: Every value in confidence must be high.
method.dedupe_gate: IDs, normalized names, aliases and external IDs checked globally; every candidate checked against all catalogue coordinates and internally at <=120 m.
method.hard_exclusions: No indoor, station, emergency, incidental attraction-access, escalator, lift, illegal, closed or technical-mountain stairs.

included.a: S Henderson Street at 42nd Avenue S, Seattle
included.s: Seattle's longest public stairway, rebuilt as a 258-step neighbourhood connector.
included.q: S Henderson Stairway Seattle United States
included.w: A 440-foot public stairway climbs 114 feet through 258 steps and 18 landings. Reopened in 2023 with lights and Seattle's longest bicycle runnel, it restores a practical connection rather than serving as an attraction entrance.

qualification.note: Official project page gives 258 steps and 114 feet of elevation gain.

facts.claim: The rebuilt public stairway is 440 feet long, gains 114 feet and contains 258 steps and 18 landings.
It reopened in 2023 with ten lights and Seattle's longest bicycle runnel as a neighbourhood connection.

included.a: Davenport Road at Spadina Road, Toronto
included.s: A civic stairway climbing the 23-metre shore cliff of vanished Lake Iroquois.
included.w: Concrete switchbacks rise 23 metres up the ancient Lake Iroquois escarpment beside Spadina Museum. Published step totals conflict, so this dossier relies on the documented ascent rather than claiming an exact count.

included.a: Brougham Street to Victoria Street, Woolloomooloo, Sydney
included.s: A 113-step 1904 harbour climb with ironwork and a Cold War dead-drop story.
included.w: Three flights and 113 steps climb more than 12 metres between Woolloomooloo and Potts Point. Built in 1904, the public stairway later entered Cold War lore as a Soviet spy dead-drop location.

qualification.note: Dictionary of Sydney documents 113 steps, three flights and more than 12 metres of climb.

facts.claim: The public stairway was built in 1904 and consists of 113 steps in three flights climbing more than 12 metres.
The steps became associated with a Soviet espionage dead drop in the Petrov affair era.
The City of Sydney still identifies the steep stairs as a public entrance route to Embarkation Park.

included.a: Edward Street to Wickham Terrace, Spring Hill, Brisbane
included.s: Ten public flights climbing from Brisbane's CBD past a wartime air-raid shelter.

facts.claim: The 1921 public stairway has ten flights and is an unusually long pedestrian connector between the CBD and Spring Hill.
A Second World War air-raid shelter forms part of the stairway's heritage setting, and the route remains used by workers and exercisers.

included.a: Burwood Highway and Mount Dandenong Tourist Road, Upper Ferntree Gully
included.s: A forest fitness climb threaded with bronze memorials to the Kokoda campaign.
included.q: Kokoda Track Memorial Walk 1000 Steps Melbourne Australia
included.w: The steep 1.4-kilometre climb known as the 1000 Steps rises through Dandenong Ranges forest past bronze Kokoda campaign plaques. It reopened after major storm repairs; scheduled 2026 night deer-control closures begin on 16 August, so check live notices.

qualification.note: 1000 Steps is an official affectionate name, not asserted here as a surveyed exact count; the documented 1.4-kilometre steep climb qualifies independently.

facts.claim: Parks Victoria describes the route as a steep 1.4-kilometre fitness climb with bronze plaques commemorating the Kokoda campaign.
The stairway reopened after storm repairs with renewed concrete steps and handrails.
Scheduled 2026 deer-control closures affect selected nights from 16 August to 19 November, not the 9 August dossier check.

The modern climb has 242 steps and is a major public fitness and endurance landmark.

included.s: A limestone passage of 66 hand-cut steps made by enslaved people in the 1790s.

facts.claim: Enslaved people hewed the limestone staircase in 1793–94 as a direct route between Nassau and Fort Fincastle.
The stair had 66 original steps; 65 are visible after later paving, and it remains presented as a public walking landmark.

included.a: Government Hill, Charlotte Amalie, St Thomas
included.s: The Caribbean step-street called 99 Steps but actually counted at 103.

facts.claim: The 18th-century step-street was built from bricks brought as ballast in Danish ships.
Despite the established name 99 Steps, the current official count is 103 and visitors are explicitly encouraged to climb them.
